result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers diagnose the problem correctly and give nearly the same values (8px/12px item padding, 8px from title to items, 24px between groups, borders removed). B wins narrowly. It puts the diagnosis first, maps each current value to its replacement in a table, uses an explicit 4px scale, and explains why the parent should own spacing and why the ratio must hold if things get denser. A ties tap-target size to legibility more directly and includes a focus ring, which B leaves out. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers spot the symmetric 4px/4px title spacing, recommend about 24px between groups versus 8px from a title to its items, remove the borders, and give similar concrete CSS. A's diagnosis is slightly sharper and includes a useful compact variant. B is a little stronger on readability and click targets: it explains the 36px row height using font size and line-height, and adds title typography and a focus ring.
